analysis:
Reviewed: evidence text files (benchmark logs, no secrets or prompt content), the calibration-prompt binary-search change, the model-calibration hook, the calibration request timeout and sampling parameter, and the new EngineV2Bridge+ShapeWarmup.swift.

Evidence files hold only timings, bundle IDs, an md5 of the binary and metallib, and short synthetic generated text, with no consumer data. Host names are anonymized. Nothing there touches the threat-model assets.

Shape warmup runs only built-in synthetic prompts (modelCalibrationPrompt, never customer data). Requests go through submitTokenized with cacheEnabled:false, so they cannot populate the SSD prefix cache (T-041). No new at-rest artifact or timing-oracle exposure results.

Warmup is gated by the same idle check, canSubmitWithNativeOwner, slotPostureClosed and foreground preemption as existing calibration. The startup preload runs before the provider registers and the listener opens (runShapeWarmupBeforeServing), so it cannot delay serving or the App Attest connection control (T-053, T-057). Its time budget is bounded by shapeWarmupBudgetSeconds via a per-cell timeout, and a cancelled task propagates. Warmup cells run with calibration semantics. The comment says no rates, buckets or counters move (per the 'warmup' cell flag), which I could not verify because ModelCalibrationPolicy is not in the supplied source.

The prompt search now probes 1 and 2, then an estimate, with bounds clamped by min(max(...,low),high). The slope division is guarded by tokens.count > one. The result stays the largest rendering that fits within targetTokens, as long as the bounds logic is right. The estimate can be a large Int, but it is clamped, so there is no overflow or crash. The temperature nil for sampled cells uses the default sampler, which is not a security-relevant change.

Open integration questions: ModelCalibrationPolicy (shapeWarmupMode, env override, shaderCacheProbe, cell.sampled) and the call sites of runShapeWarmupBeforeServing are not supplied, so I cannot confirm the default-off or default-on mode. The TB-011 posture and the serving-authorization ordering around the startup preload were also not verified.
